notes: Main commercial port. Handles approximately $2.1B in annual cargo. Scenario A: reduced throughput with crane restrictions. Scenario B: full suspension — life safety risk from storm surge and extreme wind. Scenario C: structural inspection required before resuming operations.

Fuel offloading terminal supplying the Avalon Peninsula. Scenario A: vessel queue forming and boom barrier at wave rating limit. Scenario B: boom barrier breached at 7.2m wave — suspension and structural risk to fuel pier. Scenario C: pier inspection required before any vessel approach.

Distribution feeder serving 18200 customers. Pre-existing degraded transformer TX-7 flagged before storm. Scenario A: monitoring elevated and crew dispatched. Scenario B: TX-7 fails under ice and wind loading — full outage. Scenario C: replacement transformer en route; 9400 customers restored via alternate feed.

High-voltage corridor supplying approximately 65000 NL customers. Scenario A: tower load monitoring elevated. Scenario B: ice accretion on Tower 14B above design threshold — backup generator pre-emptively activated; repair crew grounded. Scenario C: repair crew en route; tower stable under remote monitoring.

Remote open-pit and underground mine. Single road access — 68 km from nearest town. Scenario A: surface ops on elevated watch and haul trucks near wind rating. Scenario B: road closed by Transport NL and helicopter suspended — 142 personnel confirmed sheltered. Scenario C: road assessment underway and helicopter window expected at 16:00.

Continuous nickel processing plant. Unplanned shutdown risks equipment damage and environmental release. Scenario A: controlled 6-hour ramp-down initiated proactively. Scenario B: fully halted and crew sheltered. Scenario C: 4-hour restart sequence initiated with environmental officer on-site.

Ferry and roll-on roll-off cargo terminal connecting passenger traffic and critical freight. Scenario B: ramp and berth operations suspended due to wind and surge exposure. Scenario C: engineering inspection required before passenger loading resumes.
Western NL bulk terminal handling salt aggregates and forestry cargo. Less exposed than Avalon sites but still affected by vessel queue spillover and equipment securing constraints during Scenario B.

Community microgrid supporting clinic refrigeration emergency shelter heat and telecom backup. Scenario B: feeder instability forces islanded operation. Scenario C: generator fuel margin becomes the limiting recovery constraint.

Water and wastewater lift station serving coastal communities. Scenario B: pump telemetry degrades under grid fluctuation. Backup generator fuel and pump runtime must be monitored to avoid service interruption.
Ore loading yard connecting remote mine output to rail transport. Scenario B: switch heater failure and drifting snow suspend loading. Scenario C: track and loader inspection gate controls restart.
Remote environmental monitoring station for tailings water level and spill detection. Scenario B: sensor degradation and satellite link dependency elevate environmental reporting risk.
